title: Hardcoded RSA Private Key in Source
description:
The RSA private key used for JWT signing is hardcoded as a string literal in the application source code, exposing it to anyone with repository access.
Scout rationale and verification strategy: Line 21 contains the full PEM-encoded RSA private key as a string constant. This key is used to sign JWTs (line 54). Anyone with source access can forge valid authentication tokens for any user, including admin. Verification: confirm the key matches the public key at line 20 and that it is used in jwt.sign at line 54.

title: MD5 Used for Password Hashing
description:
The hash function uses MD5, a cryptographically broken algorithm, making stored password hashes vulnerable to collision and rainbow-table attacks.
Scout rationale and verification strategy: Line 41 defines hash() using crypto.createHash('md5'). MD5 is not collision-resistant and is trivially brute-forced. If this function is used for password storage, an attacker who obtains the database can recover plaintext passwords. Verification: confirm where hash() is called in the registration/login flow to determine if it applies to user passwords.

title: Open Redirect via Weak Allowlist Check
description:
The isRedirectAllowed function uses String.includes() to validate redirect URLs against an allowlist, which can be bypassed by appending the allowed URL as a substring of a malicious domain.
Scout rationale and verification strategy: Line 136 checks url.includes(allowedUrl), so a URL like 'https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop.evil.com' would pass validation because it contains the allowed string as a substring. This allows redirecting users to attacker-controlled domains. Verification: call the redirect endpoint with a URL that contains an allowlisted string as a substring of a different domain.

observations.title: SQL Injection in Product Search
observations.description: User-controlled query parameter 'q' is directly interpolated into a raw SQL query string without parameterization or escaping, allowing arbitrary SQL injection.
observations.rationale: Line 21 reads req.query.q into 'criteria', line 22 only truncates length to 200 chars, and line 23 concatenates it directly into a sequelize.query() string. No parameterized query or escaping is applied. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the 'q' parameter. Verification: send a harmless tautology like q=' OR '1'='1 to confirm the query executes injected logic.
